capabilities.description: Bounded extended-grapheme editing and atomic replacement
guarantees: UTF-8 storage and grapheme cursor boundaries; display cells are distinct from byte offsets
Atomic capacity/control/range rejection; no host language interpretation

capabilities.description: In-memory history mechanics with exact unsent-draft return
guarantees: Host explicitly admits entries and owns persistence, retention and privacy
Up/Down preserve the original draft and cursor

capabilities.description: Event-driven host completion requests and validated replacement
guarantees: Host owns candidate discovery and selection; replacement validates grapheme ranges

capabilities.description: Synchronous safe plain output coordinated with an active draft
guarantees: Exact draft/cursor restoration; safe controls and terminal cleanup
No concurrent independent writers; host owns output meaning

capabilities.description: Simple accented prompt, optional literal state and continuation
guarantees: Prompt::new remains simple; safe control-free labels
Terminal-default background; NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb disable styling

capabilities.description: Exact pre-release C ABI 1 with caller-owned spans/buffers and opaque handles
guarantees: Numeric ABI identity 1; layout and symbol contract qualified
Static/shared installation; caller descriptors are duplicated, not transferred
No long-term stability or Windows resource-binding claim

capabilities.description: Qualified Linux terminal resource binding
guarantees: Exact termios restoration, paste lifecycle, resource exclusion and descriptor ownership
Real Rust/C PTYs and Linux Valgrind qualification

capabilities.description: Qualified macOS terminal resource binding through the shared POSIX backend
guarantees: Real Rust/C PTYs and native leak qualification; captured console modes restored

capabilities.description: Platform-neutral editing, interaction state and logical rendering
guarantees: Native Linux/macOS/Windows portable tests; Windows has no runtime terminal backend
No operating-system resources, scheduler or product semantics in the engine

capabilities.description: Safe semantic documents, inline spans, headings, facts, lists, literals and separators
guarantees: Document::render/write_to work without an editor; Interaction::output_document coordinates an active POSIX draft
Bounded input/work; no terminal control injection or silent truncation
Plain, NO_COLOR and dumb output retain structure; wrapping uses grapheme/cell geometry

capabilities.description: Responsive line-oriented tables over safe structured text
guarantees: Unicode cell alignment, bounded column shrinking and multiline cells
Narrow layouts stack records; no horizontal scrolling or hidden content

capabilities.description: Generic severity notices with explicit non-color markers
guarantees: Info, success, warning and error remain distinct without color
Host supplies classification; no application status ontology

capabilities.description: Ordered safe styled segments for primary and continuation prompts
guarantees: Prompt::composed and with_continuation_text share Text/Span geometry
The simple Prompt::new and C ABI 1 prompt remain unchanged

capabilities.description: Explicit role-to-foreground/emphasis mapping
guarantees: Style and Foreground accept no terminal escapes; default background is retained
Explicit Default overrides block emphasis; unstyled Text inherits block defaults
Existing palette and color-disable policies remain compatible

capabilities.description: Retained blocking read with typed submission, editing interrupt and EOF
guarantees: One engine and resource lifecycle; no host poll loop required
History admission and application meaning remain host-owned; no completion discovery

capabilities.description: Explicit session compatibility over the common driver
guarantees: Existing open/poll/completion/output/close behavior and bounded read-ahead remain available
Compatibility polling retains bounded periodic resize observation; C ABI 1 unchanged

capabilities.description: Externally scheduled input, opaque deadlines and resize over one engine
guarantees: No periodic library wake when idle without a deadline; no blocking input-ready advancement
Host owns event waiting and resize notification; output mutations remain serialized
Deadline tokens reject early, stale and previous-session notifications

capabilities.description: Borrowed native readiness with portable scheduling vocabulary
guarantees: Linux/macOS input source is borrowed and cannot transfer resource/restoration ownership
POSIX registration must end before close/reopen; generic wake types contain no descriptors

capabilities.description: Unified terminal admission across blocking, session and driven embedding
guarantees: Native resource observations override protocol configuration; negative admission precedes raw mode and output
TERM is a protocol hint; NO_COLOR is user policy, captured at configuration boundaries
Presentation, Editing and Driven requirements share one resolver; optional styling and paste degrade explicitly
No-paste ordinary editing does not promise atomic multiline input; missing native geometry reports CapabilityMismatch
Legacy session/C ABI 1 retains explicit VT assumptions and unchanged numeric C admission status

capabilities.description: Inspectable portable facts, requirements and resolved capability snapshot
guarantees: Observed resource facts, protocol assumptions, optional policy and degradation remain distinct
Dimension query, resize delivery, waitable readiness and protocol deadlines are independent
Native active snapshot inspection performs no I/O; generic resolution has no allocation or environment reads
Windows qualifies the portable model only; no terminal runtime is supplied

capabilities.description: Public deterministic display-cell policy over the shared presentation implementation
guarantees: UnicodeNarrow preserves the qualified unicode-width non-CJK policy for safe single-line text
UTF-8 validity, grapheme segmentation and display cells are separate; control text is rejected by the width query
Actual emulator/font emoji and ambiguous-width behavior is not discovered or universally guaranteed

capabilities.description: Immutable revision-identified draft snapshots and atomic stale-result refusal
guarantees: One opaque identity scoped to the originating retained Editor; successful text/cursor changes advance, no-ops and rejected edits do not
Submit, editing interrupt and EOF end the semantic draft; unchanged close/reopen, resize and coordinated output preserve draft provenance
Snapshots own immutable shared text, cursor and revision; hosts own all parsing, context, scheduling and derived payloads
Revision-bound replacement refuses stale results before validation or mutation, without history or terminal output effects
Checked 128-bit exhaustion panics before mutation rather than wrapping; unrelated editors are separate identity domains
Rust Editor is portable; native Interaction completion is qualified on Linux/macOS; C ABI 1 remains synchronous and unchanged

capabilities.description: Bounded host-ordered revision-bound completion candidates
guarantees: Hosts own discovery, order, ranking, application context and scheduling; no callback or executor is acquired
Per-candidate grapheme-aligned ranges, insertion, safe label and optional annotation are distinct; duplicates preserve host order
Sets bind the originating Editor DraftRevision; stale delivery refuses before validation or activation with zero terminal bytes
Whole-set validation is atomic; 4096 candidates, 65536 bytes per field and 4 MiB aggregate safe text are bounded
Same-revision explicit deliveries replace in delivery order; host request preference is not inferred
C ABI 1 retains its synchronous request/replacement contract unchanged

capabilities.description: Safe responsive temporary candidate selection through the shared renderer
guarantees: Nonempty sets require explicit acceptance; zero candidates silently dismiss; selection never previews by mutating the draft
Tab/Shift-Tab navigate in host order; Enter accepts, Escape dismisses through the existing decoder deadline; arrows retain editing/history
Acceptance uses atomic revision-bound replacement; changed drafts dismiss candidates, no-op/rejected edits preserve current state
Resize and serialized external output restore exact draft/cursor/selection without changing revision
At most eight temporary rows, selected index/count and a textual selection marker preserve plain usability; labels/annotations may ellipsize without changing insertion
One engine/frame-transition renderer and existing F2 width/theme/admission model; Linux/macOS native runtime, Windows portable logic only

changes.description: Bounded host-ordered revision-bound completion candidates. Host discovery and scheduling stay external; no consumer migration is assigned and C ABI 1 remains unchanged.
Safe responsive temporary candidate selection through the shared renderer. Host discovery and scheduling stay external; no consumer migration is assigned and C ABI 1 remains unchanged.
